bodyEn: Having finally got the title monkey off our back, and with much of the competition in a state of flux, there’s plenty of optimism. Obviously the target is for Arteta to sustain the same appetite and intensity to mount a credible defence. The big questions are whether we can reproduce the same resilience at the back with Saliba on the long-term missing list, and will the introduction of Guimarães be the catalyst for the sort of midfield chemistry we’ll need to carve open opponents who plan to park the bus?

Key players/weak links On the evidence of our pre-season outings we urgently need the return of our remaining World Cup stars – Rice, Zubimendi and Saka should provide a renewed sense of purpose, both to counter any defensive fragility and to increase our goal threat. We’re all hoping for a breakthrough season for a beefed-up Max Dowman, and are anxious to discover if Tzolis is an upgrade on Trossard.

We still need to sign … Our friendly outings have shown the need for alternative attacking options, such as Atlético’s Julián Alvarez, and cover for Saliba – Quansah and Konsa are linked. But presumably any further arrivals will be dependent on some astute pruning of those who’ve failed to cut the mustard, such as Vieira and Nelson.

Our cult hero is … Benny Blanco’s off-the-ball shenanigans ensure that he’s enshrined as a firm terrace favourite, but it’s the demeanour of Declan Rice that will invariably set the tone for whether or not we’re destined for more success.
If we could sign two players from our past … Who wouldn’t want to add the artistry of Thierry Henry and Dennis Bergkamp to any team?
We will finish 1st. Top four: 1. Arsenal; 2. Chelsea; 3. Manchester City; 4. Liverpool. Bottom three: 18. Coventry; 19. Ipswich; 20. Hull. First manager sacked Sergej Jakirovic.
Bernard Azulay onlinegooner.com; @GoonerN5

It would be daft to not be optimistic when each year under Emery we’ve created great memories, regardless of the previous summer’s transfer merry-go-round. Top six and a cup run of any flavour would count as a good season, and it may be that our best moments are back-end weighted as we integrate some exciting new talent. I understand that Manzambi is the best thing to come out of Switzerland since the cuckoo clock, and any 22-year-old with 187 senior appearances (Garnacho) must be all right. Perversely, the financial regulations that are holding us back should prevent too much moaning if we don’t get off to a flyer, and having a ground with only three sides might even help us make VP a fortress. In all, I’m fired up for the new season.

Key players/weak links The senior pros all need to keep drinking the Emery Kool Aid, but why wouldn’t they? Konsa remains a colossus and the purple prose around McGinn is fully deserved. If Kamara plays 40 senior games and not his usual 25 it will improve our finishing spot by two. Normally naming a young player to watch in these pages guarantees them a loan move to Lincoln, but Brian Madjo has looked immense up front in pre-season.
We still need to sign … Marcus Rashford.

Our cult hero is … McGinn must already have done enough to have a hospitality suite named after him. Another two years and it could be a stand. He will be aware that Emery doesn’t deal in sentimentality so I expect yet another year in which SJM pushes for player of the season while being a key figure in the dressing room.
If we could sign two players from our past … Dwight Yorke, from 1995-96 when he switched to an out-and-out striker. And Gareth Barry: the complete midfielder.
We will finish 6th. Top four: 1. Arsenal; 2. Manchester City; 3. Manchester United; 4. Chelsea. Bottom three: 18. Fulham; 19. Ipswich; 20. Hull. First manager sacked Roberto De Zerbi.
Jonathan Pritchard

We’re so looking forward to this: our first ever season in a European club competition. It’s going to be monumental. And, with arguably our strongest ever squad to call on, we expect to be competitive in the Europa League too. We’re excited to see Marco Rose in charge and a continuation of the fast, attacking, no-fear brand of football that earned us our highest ever finish last season. In view of the extra games we have on the schedule, a mid-table Premier League finish would be very respectable, but winning a trophy feels weirdly achievable. Why not a European one?

Key players/weak links António Silva has big Senesi-sized shoes to fill at centre-half but we expect big things from him. We’re also looking forward to the impact that new striker Álvaro Rodríguez and the attacking right-back Juanlu will bring. Watch out too for a fully fit Ben Gannon-Doak – a breakthrough season beckons for him.
We still need to sign … Business is pretty much done. We’re in a good place, with maybe one or two to go out on loan deals towards the end of the window.

Our cult hero is … Long-serving veteran defender Adam Smith continues to perform at the highest level, an incredible 16 years after his debut for the club. He epitomises the journey we’ve been on and we love him for it.

If we could sign two players from our past … It would be hard to turn down a peak Nathan Aké or Callum Wilson, but then with the squad that we have now, I’m not convinced they would get into a starting 11. Perhaps, with Junior Kroupi out for a few months, there might be a place for a natural finisher like Jermain Defoe. Better still, prime Ted MacDougall would score hatfuls every week in this team.
We will finish 12th. Top four: 1. Manchester City; 2. Arsenal; 3. Liverpool; 4. Manchester United. Bottom three: 18. Hull; 19. Ipswich; 20. Leeds. First manager sacked Xabi Alonso.
Jeff Hayward Back of the Net, the AFC Bournemouth Fan’s Podcast

I’m very optimistic. Twelve months ago we had Yoane Wissa refusing to train to force a move and the footballing world was convinced that our free-kick coach turned manager would get us relegated. Fast forward a year and things feel very different. We’ve had a proper pre-season, there’s a clear tactical approach and, importantly, we’ve signed players who can actually execute it. The target? Keep improving. If we can get a European spot this season, that would be another sign that we’re moving forward year-on-year. For a club like Brentford, that’s a pretty exciting prospect.

Key players/weak links There’s a lot of excitement around new signing Mamadou Sangaré – so much so that he’s already got his own song. Callum Wilson is a shrewd signing too, and, at this stage of his career, seems happy to sit on the bench and knock a few in when called upon. Our explosive front three of Ouattara, Thiago and Schade have now had time to gel, and should cause plenty of problems. As for youngsters, 11 players aged 21 or under are vying for a place in the final 25-man squad. 19-year-old striker – and rapper – Kaye Furo is highly rated, as is 20-year-old centre-back Jannik Schuster. It’s a good sign that we’re getting to the point where our youngsters aren’t just making up the numbers.
We still need to sign … If there’s one position we could strengthen, left-back would be a good option. El Hadji Malick Diouf from West Ham has been rumoured.
Our cult hero is … Michael Kayode. Cemented his status by singing his own terrace chant on camera: “He eats spaghetti, he drinks Moretti, he hates Queens Park Rangers.”

If we could sign two players from our past … We’re probably a bit too “nice”. Whenever we need a short injection of old-school fire, fight and chaos, Terry Evans from our 1992 Division One-winning side and Terry Hurlock from that incredible 80s “Kamara, Bowles, Hurlock” midfield would be great to call upon.

We will finish 6th. Top four: 1. Manchester City; 2. Arsenal; 3. Manchester United; 4. Bournemouth. Bottom three: 18. Fulham; 19. Ipswich; 20. Hull. First manager sacked I got it spot-on last season, predicting two consecutive Forest sackings. Surely Glasner isn’t next on the cards? OK, go on then …
Billy Grant Beesotted podcast and blog; @Beesotted; @BillyTheBee99

Having seen West Ham, Chelsea and even Crystal Palace go all the way in the Conference League, the main target is doing well in that and winning a first cup final since the 1910 Charity Shield. Am I optimistic about it happening? Not really. The competition looks tougher this year. Freiburg, Atalanta and Monaco all have proper European experience. Even the playoff round against Tromsø is a banana skin. I’m old enough to remember some pretty horrible trips to Carlisle when Brighton could never win north of Lake Windermere. Let alone inside the actual Arctic Circle.

Key players/weak links The key player will be whoever Fabian Hürzeler uses to fill the void left by selling Danny Welbeck: Georginio Rutter, Charalampos Kostoulas or Stefanos Tzimas. Not only did Welbeck score 13 goals last season, but most were vital equalisers or important winners worth 13 points. Allowing him to join Chelsea is a huge risk. If none of those younger alternatives who the club want playing more this season step up and replace Welbeck, there’s the weak link. And there are big question marks over all three.
We still need to sign … Danny Welbeck from Chelsea would be a good signing for his goals record and the experience he would bring to a young squad.

Our cult hero is … Rutter. Nothing says cult hero quite like having one Instagram account about your football career and another about the racehorses you own. With the racing one being more interesting.

If we could sign two players from our past … I’ll spare you another Welbeck answer and say Glenn Murray and Bobby Zamora instead. Hopefully, I’ll be able to revisit this on 3 June 2027 after we’ve just won the Conference League and Kostoulas has hit 46 goals in all competitions. Danny who?
We will finish 13th. Top four: 1. Arsenal; 2. Manchester United; 3. Manchester City; 4. Chelsea; Bottom three: 18. Sunderland; 19. Ipswich; 20. Hull. First manager sacked Oliver Glasner.
Scott McCarthy WeAreBrighton.com

A new top manager, some decent new signings and a feelgood factor within the squad – it’s hard not to be optimistic. We’ve finally brought some experienced players who should complement our younger players and take them to the next level. With no Champions League football, the target has to be top four and a good run in the domestic cups.

Key players/weak links We’ve strengthened in most areas so it’s key that the new signings make a quick impact. Palmer and Colwill will hopefully have fully recovered, too, and will hit the floor running. Really looking forward to seeing Morgan Rogers in a blue shirt and Marco Palestra looks promising. I still worry with Sánchez in goal, though, and Penders might be a bit green for the Premier League. As for youngsters, I’d add Reggie Watson to the squad as a wildcard. He impressed in pre-season, giving off real John Terry vibes. How is he only 16?

We still need to sign … If Enzo Fernández goes he’ll need replacing; Alex Scott and Adam Wharton have both been heavily linked and either would be a good choice, adding to the English spine of the team. The rest of the squad looks very balanced with strength in depth. At this stage of the window the main focus will be on trimming the squad to a manageable level.

Our cult hero is … In a team with few real characters I’m hoping some of the new signings will shake the squad up a bit. I’ve a feeling Pep Chavarría could quickly become a fan favourite with some dark arts. Cole Palmer will continue to entertain on and off the pitch with his great interviews.

If we could sign two players from our past … John Terry to marshal the defence and Frank Lampard to bang the goals in. Both players gave 100% every time they stepped on the pitch and were also fantastic motivators. Two absolute legends who would grace any team in any era.
We will finish Fourth. Top four: 1. Arsenal; 2. Manchester United; 3. Manchester City; 4. Chelsea. Bottom three: 18. Newcastle; 19. Ipswich; 20. Hull. First manager sacked Sergej Jakirovic.
Paul Baker in memory of Trizia Fiorellino

There’s no downside to choosing optimism, so yes, we’re optimistic. I don’t expect a top-half finish but I do enjoy how the club’s being run and believe in our ability to compete. Clearly the target is to survive, but within that, if we can showcase what’s good about us and provide a challenge, that would be a very acceptable return.

Key players/weak links The money we’ve spent is basically unfathomable, but my focus has been on those who were so critical to our promotion. Matt Grimes connects everyone in the team so we’re relying on him doing that again, else we’ll have to develop a completely new way to function. Signing keeper Carl Rushworth also gives assurance at the back that we hope will translate into points. There are questions about our strikers (which feels barmy for a team that scored 99 goals last season). It’s not complicated – we simply don’t know if Wright and Simms have what it takes to score at the highest level. Aside from signing Aurèle Amenda, we haven’t touched our defence either. It’s a bold strategy. Liam Kitching and Jay Dasilva have improved significantly, but it’s hard to ignore the notion that we’re relying on players like this finding another uptick. However, new signing Caleb Yirenkyi looks very special.

We still need to sign … We saw how vital Brian Brobbey was for Sunderland last season. A dynamic, high-status striker would go a long way towards calming the nerves about our forward line. Is Taiwo Awoniyi able to be that guy? Let’s hope so. The rumours about Fikayo Tomori are exciting. If we could bring him in, good lord.

Our cult hero is … While the returning Gus Hamer is clearly our cult hero, Milan van Ewijk is the joker of the team. You’ll find him front and centre of every celebration. But don’t let the daftness fool you; he’s a serious, serious player.

If we could sign two players from our past … The original version of James Maddison was unlike anything I’ve ever seen. His game has adapted with age, which is a shame, but I’d love some of that early ingenuity. I’d also welcome back Viktor Gyökeres. He functions far better when he believes he’s the star man. Come home Vik and bash your way to upwards of nine Premier League goals for Coventry.
We will finish 17th. Top four: 1. Manchester City, 2. Chelsea, 3. Arsenal, 4. Manchester United. Bottom three: 18. Ipswich, 19. Fulham, 20. Hull. First manager sacked Daniel Farke.
Neil Allison @skybluesblog, Nii Lamptey Show Podcast

What are we expecting? Right now, it’s really difficult to say. The only key player to have exited (so far) is Maxence Lacroix, on whom we made a massive profit, but we still have to strengthen the squad so that it can cope with the rigours of going deep in the Europa League without risking our Premier League campaign – a lesson learned from last season. Lots of incoming deals seem close, but not yet over the line.

Key players/weak links Ismaïla Sarr and J-P Mateta will once again be essential, given the lack of goals in the rest of the squad. Adam Wharton will show how insane it was for Tuchel to leave him out of the World Cup, and Tyrick Mitchell will continue to excel on the left. Jaydee Canvot, still only 20, is destined to be a superb centre-back and should grow further in stature this season.

We still need to sign … There’s been some solid business already – US teenager Zavier Gozo and right-back Anan Khalaili look exciting prospects, and Evann Guessand is welcome back from Villa. But we still need a replacement for Lacroix, and strength in the middle – we had a £35m bid for Monaco’s Lamine Camara rejected. Plenty still to do. Meanwhile, the decision to swap Dwight McNeil for Brennan Johnson has split opinion: Johnson – all £35m of him – was only here a few months.

Our cult hero is … A few contenders. Mateta, obviously, chant-leader Dean Henderson and, potentially, our Brazilian attacker Matheus França. He’s not there yet, but he joined the club three years ago at 19 and has barely made an impact for various reasons. But he’s had a strong pre-season, including dancing goal celebrations – some Brazilian flair would go down very well at Selhurst.

If we could sign two players from our past … Michael Olise without a doubt; he was clearly a world-class player at Palace and has continued to progress spectacularly. And Matt Jansen, from the late 90s – a personal hero of mine; such incredible talent at such a young age and would shine in the modern era.
We will finish 14th. Top four: 1. Arsenal; 2. Manchester City; 3. Chelsea; 4. Tottenham. Bottom three: 18. Newcastle; 19. Ipswich; 20. Hull; First manager sacked Matthias Jaissle.
Chris Waters @Clapham_Grand

Despite the £327m the Friedkins have provided since the takeover, there are still doubts about the scale of their ambition. Recruitment is tough, the process (Moyes or committee as decision-makers) is uncertain. Realistically, aiming for eighth (and European qualification) is the likely limit. Does that make Blues feel optimistic? Unlikely. The 31-year wait for a trophy hangs heavy on our hearts and minds.

Key players/weak links Midfield is looking stronger but can Beto/Barry score 20 goals between them? Tyrique George (acquired from Chelsea) is a key signing. The right side of the pitch remains problematic. A couple of youngsters to watch: Harrison Armstrong, 19, made his breakthrough last season, and, even younger at 18, Braiden Graham, the Northern Ireland forward signed from Linfield.

We still need to sign … A right-back. Jake O’Brien, who has been covering there, is a fabulous centre-back and would be perfect in the middle alongside Branthwaite. A proven goalscorer would be a bonus, as would a right-winger.

Our cult hero is … Jordan Pickford. His contribution to Everton maintaining top-flight status and his excellence in goal for England are shamefully under-reported in the media. We are blessed to have such a dedicated player who loves playing for his country, the club and his fans.

If we could sign two players from our past … Alan Ball, the best outfield player to play for the club in my opinion, never stopped running, commanded midfield, was skilful and a great passer and had a tremendous shot – he had it all, and would walk into any Premier League side of any generation. What would he be worth today? And a 17-year-old Wayne Rooney.

We will finish I said eighth last season, the optimist says eighth again. But realistically, 10th. Top four: 1. Arsenal; 2. Liverpool; 3. Manchester United; 4. Aston Villa. Bottom three: 18. Tottenham; 19. Coventry; 20. Hull. First manager sacked Oliver Glasner, not because he deserves it, but because of the owner.
Paul Quinn @theesk, theesk.org

I’m always optimistic at this stage of the summer – but there’s a bit of trepidation mixed in this time round. How on earth do you make an informed judgment on our chances when so much has changed? It’s farewell (and thanks) to Marco Silva and a warm welcome to Álvaro Arbeloa, who brings with him a new set of backroom staff, a fresh approach and a determination to write a new chapter. Seems we’re set for a new, dynamic strategy, one that’ll keep us on the edge of our seats. In a good way, hopefully.

Key players/weak links We expect striker Gonzalo García (22) and versatile midfielder César Palacios (21) to hit the ground running. The Spanish duo have followed their former boss from Real Madrid knowing that running hard is part of the deal. Another midfielder, Shea Charles (22), also joined the fold, and, as well as helping to lower the average age of the squad, the trio will be eager to discard their “promising” tags by excelling in the top flight. Arbeloa may well turn to the youth ranks too, with 18-year-old winger Macaulay Zepa one to watch.
We still need to sign … If Arbeloa gets his way there’ll be further additions, probably to freshen up the back four. And maybe a younger keeper who’s good with his feet to take over from Leno.

Our cult hero is … For humour, the Naija Boys – Iwobi and Bassey – who will no doubt continue their off-pitch antics and comedic Instagram stories, although they’re a man light now that Chukwueze has headed back to Milan. Unless someone else steps up, captain Tom Cairney remains the main man, still capable of scoring match-winning worldies after parking his antique bath chair at the side of the pitch.
If we could sign two players from our past … Obvious goal-getter up front would be Louis Saha. And the super-strong Mousa Dembélé bossing things in central midfield would suit AA’s style perfectly.
We will finish 14th. Top four: 1. Arsenal; 2. Manchester City; 3. Manchester United; 4. Chelsea. Bottom three: 18. Coventry; 19. Ipswich; 20. Hull. First manager sacked Matthias Jaissle.
David Lloyd @DMLTOOFIF

I’m very optimistic. Sure, chances are that we’ll get relegated but we’ll certainly not be the pushovers people are expecting us to be. We thrive when we’re being written off, as last season showed, and have a pragmatic manager who has us playing brilliant, transitional football which suits the Premier League. We could definitely upset a lot of teams and maybe, just maybe, even stay up.

Key players/weak links As the squad currently stands, Oli McBurnie, Mohamed Belloumi and Charlie Hughes will be the key faces. But with new signings arriving to add some much-needed experience and necessary skill, that may change. Hidemasa Morita has been an absolute coup on a free, so he may be one to keep an eye on. Full-back is still a problem position for us: there’s only Ryan Giles on the left and questions over Lewie Coyle and Cody Drameh at this level on the right. Thanks to a late flurry in the window we’ve now got a healthy plethora of young talent hoping to break through. 18-year-old Australian Lucas Herrington comes as a fully fledged international and had the likes of Barcelona sniffing around before signing for us.

We still need to sign … We still really need depth in the full-back areas and desperately need a forward or two to compete with McBurnie. We could do with some more Premier League experience across the back line, too, as well as another back-up goalkeeper thanks to Jack Butland’s lengthy injury.
Our cult hero is … Definitely McBurnie. He’s a handful for every defender and a constant wind-up merchant. The kind of player you hate to be against but love to have in your team.

If we could sign two players from our past … I would have Jarrod Bowen on the wing and Andy Robertson in at left-back. Strangely, they were two transfers I thought might actually happen this summer following West Ham’s relegation and Robertson leaving Liverpool on a free. Alas, it wasn’t to be.
We will finish 17th. Top four: 1. Arsenal; 2. Man City; 3. Liverpool; 4. Man United. Bottom three: 18. Crystal Palace; 19. Ipswich; 20. Coventry. First manager sacked Frank Lampard.
Ant Northgraves To Hull & Back Podcast

Having endured the Premier League two years ago, the fans know what to expect: eyes are well and truly open. The momentum and hope we had two seasons ago was stopped in its tracks pretty swiftly once the season started. This time round, the summer’s transfer business looks of a better quality, more robust, a step up in quality, giving us half a chance of survival and a smidge of optimism.

Key players/weak links Sasa Lukic looks to be exactly the type of signing we need to be making. 30 years old, good Premier League experience to add some no-nonsense mettle and physicality. There will need to be more like him and Issa Diop through the spine of the team. One youngster to watch: Sindre Walle Egeli has just turned 20, and signed for a Championship record fee of £17.5m last August. He had an up-and-down season but has had a really good pre-season in the No 10 role.

We still need to sign … A senior striker, to take the pressure off our new, young Brazilian forward Emersonn, who was Gary O’Neil’s first signing when he joined from Toulouse for £25m in July. We were strongly linked with Callum Wilson before he went to Brentford. I do wonder whether we’ll get to the end of August and land Zian Flemming from Burnley.

Our cult hero is … Of the current players, Marcelino Núñez is probably the closest. He has plenty of credit in the bank after his transfer, last summer, from a lower league club. That said, Florentino Luís’s early social media posts mean he has serious potential in this category. We’ve already had AI farmers and Suffolk Punches on Insta & TikTok …

If we could sign two players from our past … Paul Mariner for his all-round presence at the top of the pitch. He would be ideal as the central striker in the modern game. And Matt Holland as a leader and box-to-box midfield general.
We will finish 16th. Top four: 1. Arsenal; 2. Manchester City; 3. Manchester United; 4. Chelsea. Bottom three: 18. Fulham; 19. Coventry; 20. Hull. First manager sacked Álvaro Arbeloa.
Craig Finbow @BlueMondayITFC; bluemondayitfc.co.uk

At the end of last season Daniel Farke challenged the owner, 49ers Enterprises, to move on from just surviving in the Premier League. So this summer Leeds have broken our transfer record for goalkeeper James “next Nigel Martyn” Trafford, paid £34m for defender Tarik Muharemovic, and gone back for Harry Wilson, one of last season’s top creators in the Premier League. Over to you, Daniel. His challenge now is turning ambition into results fast enough to prove he’s the manager to move Leeds on from just surviving. A long-lusted-for new West Stand is under construction at Elland Road and the mood is good, which can be dangerous for a self-professed massive club in the bottom half of the Premier League.

Key players/weak links The main strength, and weakness, is Dominic Calvert-Lewin. He’s our key goalscorer, but doesn’t have much back-up. Left-back is similar, but Jayden Lienou is a promising teenage understudy for Gabriel Gudmundsson.
We still need to sign … The priority is a striker to help Calvert-Lewin and Lukas Nmecha. There are rumours, though, about adding more flair for the forward line.

Our cult hero is … Anton Stach’s YouTube channel is, thankfully, a delightful contribution to happiness in our world. He’s been wandering the streets of Leeds incognito asking people what they have for breakfast, and filming himself buying EU plug adaptors in Boots. On Instagram, his partner’s gameday graphics have brought Sharknados to Elland Road. Good, wholesome stuff.
If we could sign two players from our past … The correct back-up for DCL would be Luciano Becchio. To add some suaveness to our bustling midfield, Gary McAllister.
We will finish 12th. Top four: 1. Arsenal; 2. Aston Villa; 3. Liverpool; 4. Manchester City. Bottom three: 18. Sunderland; 19. Hull; 20. Coventry. First manager sacked Frank Lampard.
Daniel Chapman leedsista.com, @leedsista.com

I’m always optimistic about a new season, but this one feels very much like a new beginning for us and a real unknown. We start minus a few familiar faces alongside a new manager and some new signings, but that’s balanced with Van Dijk and Alisson still being here and others who’ve been at the club a while now. I’d put little store by the pre-season results or that Iraola said we can’t run after 60 minutes – he didn’t mean it – and we’ll see how it goes when it all kicks off for real next week. We have top players, the boss comes with a style that fits in with the club and I believe we’ll do well. The target is to be up there fighting for a top spot next May.

Key players/weak links At the back with all their experience, Van Dijk and Alisson will be crucial. There’s a big gap to fill up front, but Isak now has the chance to stake his claim after a nightmare season for him last time around. Wirtz too will want to show he can adapt to the pace of the Premier League and be a force. As for youngsters, Rio Ngumoha has already shown what he can do and the more he plays the better he will become. Trey Nyoni is pulling in the plaudits for his midfield play and if Giovanni Leoni continues his recovery he too has the potential to nail down a place.

We still need to sign … Defenders. Despite bringing in a couple, including Ifeanyi Ndukwe who won’t count yet, it still feels as if we need a solid centre-back and right-back for the immediate and long-term future. Konsa or Murillo at Forest? A central midfielder to help out Gravenberch and an attacker who plays on the right – Ibrahim Mbaye has been mooted, though PSG might balk at the idea of us coming after two players, because Barcola is a done deal. Apparently.
Our cult hero is … Not sure we have one at the minute, we need someone to step up.
If we could sign two players from our past … Alan Hansen to partner Van Dijk, and Steven Gerrard to inspire and work his magic from midfield all over the pitch.
We will finish 1st. Top four: 1. Liverpool; 2. Arsenal; 3. Chelsea; 4. Manchester City. Bottom three: 18. Nottingham Forest; 19. Ipswich; 20. Hull. First manager sacked Pierre Sage.
Steph Jones

I’m excited; it’s a new dawn under Maresca. Naturally, every City fan loved Pep’s reign. We know we’ll never have it as good again. And I doubt we’ll ever see a more dominant managerial era in the Premier League. But after 10 years, naturally, there’s something exciting about a fresh start. The target is simple: we need to win the league back. The last team that weren’t City to retain the title were United in 2008-09. It’s our job to make it incredibly difficult for Arsenal.

Key players/weak links To temper the optimism slightly, losing Rodri, if it happens, is obviously a massive blow. He’s the best No 6 in the world, without doubt. So by definition, he’s irreplaceable. Having said that, given his age (30), the club were always planning to sign his successor this summer. And in adding Anderson and Bouaddi, it feels like Viana has done excellent business. The key players will be Haaland, Semenyo, Gvardiol, Donnarumma, O’Reilly, Cherki, Foden (if he can recover his level) and Doku. They’re the most nailed-on starters (plus Anderson). Youngster to watch? Ryan McAidoo.

We still need to sign … We’re still lacking depth out wide. McAidoo looks really promising. But if Doku or Semenyo pick up an injury, then currently (pending the Spurs interest) we’d have to rely on Savinho. He’d burnt most City fans’ heads out last season … so much natural talent, but an infuriating lack of end product. Hopefully we upgrade him if he goes. Right-back is also a concern for me: too much depends on Nunes (again).
Our cult hero is … Has to be Haaland, doesn’t it? The bloke’s dripping in aura. The manner in which he schooled Gabriel v Brazil at the World Cup … delicious. More of that please.

If we could sign two players from our past … Raheem Sterling was ridiculously good in his prime. Just relentless. He’d be perfect for Maresca’s system, with wingers isolated one-v-one. And Aymeric Laporte: vastly underrated, I think he’s still good enough to play for us!
We will finish 2nd. Top four: 1. Arsenal; 2. Manchester City; 3. Chelsea; 4. Tottenham. Bottom three: 18. Fulham; 19. Ipswich; 20. Hull. First manager sacked Sergej Jakirovic.
Lloyd Scragg 9320pod.com; @lloyd_scragg

Carrick is getting the best out of a group who were spectacularly mismanaged for a couple of years. The difference he made in six months was ridiculous. After the longest goodbye in recent history, Casemiro has gone, replaced by midfielders who can actually run – but we could still be reliant on keeping injury-prone Mount fit. I hope it’s not a case of Glazernomics repeating itself, where we spend to qualify for the Champions League, then go shopping in the bargain bin once we’ve qualified. Give Carrick another couple of decent signings and I genuinely think we can challenge: Arsenal fell over the line, City have lost their greatest-ever manager, Liverpool’s defence already looks shot through and Chelsea have 35 first-team players, which should present its own problems. Realistically, I think we will finish third.

Key players/weak links We are looking forward to the link-up play between Tielemans and Bruno. Tielemans’s eye for a pass will be a boon for our forwards. I can see Sesko building on a decent first season but if we’re competing on four fronts we need to sign another striker. The weak spot is still left-back. Luke Shaw being fit was almost a miracle last season, but we can’t build a season around hoping his body holds together.

We still need to sign … A left-back, Lewis Hall would be my choice. We need another striker, we will probably get last-resort Watkins on the last day of the window, hopefully a straight swap for Rashford.

Our cult hero is … Carrick. He went from being the quiet bloke in the background to dragging United into the Champions League. There’s something very satisfying about a former United player coming back and actually understanding what the club is supposed to be.

If we could sign two players from our past … Robson and Rooney. Captain Marvel in midfield for the leadership, aggression and sheer refusal to accept defeat. Rooney because he was everything you want from a modern forward: technically brilliant, ferocious, selfless and capable of playing anywhere on the pitch.

We will finish 3rd. Top four: 1. Arsenal; 2. Manchester City; 3. Manchester United; 4. Liverpool. Bottom three: 18. Sunderland; 19. Leeds; 20. Ipswich. First manager sacked Oliver Glasner: gone before Halloween.
Shaun O’Donnell

We’re hurting. We’ve lost our most successful manager in decades, plus his talismanic captain. A-listers have departed and we’ve been humiliated in the transfer market, for the second summer running. Yes, a reset was needed, but we weren’t expecting it to be like this. At least, in Matthias Jaissle, we have a hungry, passionate young manager whose intensity will be welcomed. He certainly looks up for the fight and, despite our outgoings, the German has some exciting talent to work with. According to CEO David Hopkinson, this is “Newcastle United 2.0”. We guess we’ll know what that means in a few months’ time.

Key players/weak links Lewis Miley is “one of our own” and, with Tonali gone, can fulfil his potential. We’ll also be expecting improvements between the posts, with Lukas Hornicek and Ewen Jaouen competing for the keeper’s jersey. And if Yoane Wissa and Anthony Elanga can replicate their World Cup form, we might have a strike force on our hands. The weak links? Joe Willock, who contributed very little to the cause last season and, sadly, Sven Botman, whose form has never recovered from his anterior cruciate ligament injury in 2024.

We still need to sign … A replacement for Bruno Guimarães, leaders on and off the field, high-grade cover at both full-back positions, a centre-half … so not too much to ask … Benfica’s versatile full-back Amar Dedić and Milan’s centre-half Fikayo Tomori would certainly be a good start. Crucially, we need to blend more experience into our youthful side, but any deals will have to be done in stealth mode, given Liverpool’s recent behaviour …
Our cult hero is … Big Dan Burn. A giant of a man, with a heart to match.

If we could sign two players from our past … Alan Shearer for his leadership and goals, and of course, the much-loved, and much-missed, Kevin Keegan. Both knew what it meant to wear the black-and-white shirt.
We will finish 10th. Top four: 1. Arsenal; 2. Manchester City; 3. Liverpool; 4. Chelsea. Bottom three: 18. Ipswich; 19. Coventry; 20. Hull. First manager sacked Álvaro Arbeloa.
David and Richard Holmes

If nothing else, it can’t be as chaotic as last season. We survived fairly comfortably in the end – thanks Vítor! – then sacked him in favour of Glasner, with the rationale being that the Austrian has won silverware. So the target this time isn’t only a decent league finish, but also something in the cabinet.

items.titleZh: 英超球迷预览：2026-27赛季逐队指南
items.summaryZh: 《卫报》球迷网络前瞻新赛季：新星、短板与首位下课主帅。阿森纳夺冠后志在卫冕，但防线与中场存疑。
bodyZh: 终于摆脱了冠军心魔，加上许多竞争对手处于变动之中，我们充满乐观。显然，目标是让阿尔特塔保持同样的渴望和强度，以进行可信的卫冕。最大的问题是，在萨利巴长期缺阵的情况下，我们能否在后防线上重现同样的韧性，以及吉马良斯的加盟能否成为我们所需的中场化学反应的催化剂，以撕开那些计划摆大巴的对手？
关键球员/弱点 从季前赛的表现来看，我们急需其余世界杯球星回归——赖斯、苏比门迪和萨卡应该带来新的目标感，既抵消防守脆弱性，又增加进球威胁。我们都希望强壮的马克斯·道曼迎来突破赛季，并急于了解齐奥利斯是否比特罗萨德更出色。
我们仍需签下…… 友谊赛表明我们需要替代进攻选择，比如马竞的胡利安·阿尔瓦雷斯，以及萨利巴的替补——夸恩萨和孔萨被联系在一起。但大概任何进一步的引援都将取决于精明地清理那些未能达到标准的人，比如维埃拉和纳尔逊。
我们的崇拜英雄是…… 本尼·布兰科的离球小动作确保了他成为看台上的宠儿，但德克兰·赖斯的举止将始终为我们是否注定取得更多成功定下基调。
如果我们能从过去签下两名球员…… 谁不想把蒂埃里·亨利和丹尼斯·博格坎普的艺术性加入任何球队？
我们将排名第一。前四：1.阿森纳；2.切尔西；3.曼城；4.利物浦。后三：18.考文垂；19.伊普斯维奇；20.赫尔城。首位下课主帅：谢尔盖·亚基罗维奇。
Bernard Azulay onlinegooner.com; @GoonerN5

在埃梅里麾下每年我们都创造美好回忆，无论上赛季的转会旋转木马如何，如果不乐观就是愚蠢的。前六名和任何形式的杯赛之旅都算好赛季，而且随着我们融入一些令人兴奋的新人才，我们的最佳时刻可能会出现在赛季后段。我听说曼赞比是瑞士自布谷鸟钟以来最棒的东西，任何22岁就有187次一线队出场（加纳乔）的人一定不错。反常的是，限制我们的财务规定应该能防止我们开局不利时抱怨太多，而且只有三面看台的球场甚至可能帮助我们把维拉公园变成堡垒。总之，我对新赛季充满期待。
关键球员/弱点 老将们都需要继续喝埃梅里的鸡汤，但他们为什么不呢？孔萨仍然是一座巨塔，对麦金的赞美完全应得。如果卡马拉打40场一线队比赛而不是通常的25场，我们的最终排名将提高两位。通常在这些版面指定一名年轻球员关注，保证他们会租借到林肯城，但布莱恩·马乔在季前赛中在前场表现巨大。
我们仍需签下…… 马库斯·拉什福德。
我们的崇拜英雄是…… 麦金一定已经做得足够多，可以有一个招待套房以他命名。再过两年，可能就是一个看台。他会知道埃默里不讲感情，所以我预计又一年SJM争夺赛季最佳球员，同时成为更衣室的关键人物。
如果我们能从过去签下两名球员…… 德怀特·约克，从1995-96赛季他转为纯粹中锋时开始。还有加雷斯·巴里：全能中场。
我们将排名第六。前四：1.阿森纳；2.曼城；3.曼联；4.切尔西。后三：18.富勒姆；19.伊普斯维奇；20.赫尔城。首位下课主帅：罗伯托·德泽尔比。
乔纳森·普里查德
我们非常期待：这是我们历史上第一个欧战赛季。这将是里程碑式的。而且，可以说拥有史上最强阵容，我们也期待在欧联杯中具有竞争力。我们很高兴看到马尔科·罗塞执教，延续上赛季为我们带来历史最高排名的快速、进攻、无畏的足球风格。鉴于赛程中额外的比赛，英超中游排名将非常可观，但赢得奖杯感觉莫名可行。为什么不拿个欧战奖杯？
关键球员/弱点 安东尼奥·席尔瓦需要填补塞内西在中卫位置上的大鞋，但我们对他寄予厚望。我们也期待新前锋阿尔瓦罗·罗德里格斯和进攻型右后卫胡安卢带来的影响。还要留意完全健康的本·甘农-多克——他的突破赛季即将到来。
我们仍需签下…… 交易基本完成。我们处于良好状态，可能有一两个在窗口末期外租。
我们的崇拜英雄是…… 长期效力的老将后卫亚当·史密斯继续在最高水平发挥，这是他首秀后令人难以置信的16年。他体现了我们走过的旅程，我们因此爱他。
如果我们能从过去签下两名球员…… 很难拒绝巅峰的纳坦·阿克或卡勒姆·威尔逊，但以我们现在的阵容，我不确定他们能进入首发11人。也许，由于朱尼尔·克鲁皮缺阵几个月，可能会有一个像杰梅因·迪福这样的天然终结者的位置。更好的是，巅峰的特德·麦克杜格尔每周都能在这支球队打进大量进球。
我们将排名第12。前四：1.曼城；2.阿森纳；3.利物浦；4.曼联。后三：18.赫尔城；19.伊普斯维奇；20.利兹联。首位下课主帅：哈维·阿隆索。
杰夫·海沃德 Back of the Net，AFC伯恩茅斯球迷播客
我非常乐观。十二个月前，约阿内·维萨拒绝训练以逼宫转会，足球界确信我们的任意球教练转型的主帅会让我们降级。一年后，情况完全不同。我们有了正常的季前赛，明确的战术方法，重要的是，我们签下了能执行战术的球员。目标？继续进步。如果我们本赛季能获得欧战席位，那将是我们逐年前进的又一迹象。对于布伦特福德这样的俱乐部，这是一个非常令人兴奋的前景。

关键球员/弱点 新援马马杜·桑加雷引起了很大兴奋——甚至已经有了自己的歌曲。卡勒姆·威尔逊也是精明的签约，在他职业生涯的这个阶段，似乎满足于坐在替补席上，需要时上场进球。我们爆炸性的前场三叉戟瓦塔拉、蒂亚戈和沙德现在有时间磨合，应该会造成很多麻烦。至于年轻人，11名21岁及以下的球员正在竞争最终25人名单的一席之地。19岁的前锋——也是说唱歌手——凯耶·富罗评价很高，20岁的中卫雅尼克·舒斯特也是如此。这是一个好迹象，我们的年轻人不再只是凑数。
我们仍需签下…… 如果有一个位置可以加强，左后卫会是不错的选择。西汉姆的埃尔哈吉·马利克·迪乌夫被传闻。
我们的崇拜英雄是…… 迈克尔·卡约德。通过在镜头前唱自己的看台歌巩固了地位：“他吃意大利面，他喝莫雷蒂，他讨厌女王公园巡游者。”
如果我们能从过去签下两名球员…… 我们可能有点太“友善”。每当我们需要一点老派的火焰、战斗和混乱时，来自1992年英甲夺冠阵容的特里·埃文斯和80年代那支不可思议的“卡马拉、鲍尔斯、赫洛克”中场的特里·赫洛克会很棒。
我们将排名第六。前四：1.曼城；2.阿森纳；3.曼联；4.伯恩茅斯。后三：18.富勒姆；19.伊普斯维奇；20.赫尔城。首位下课主帅 上赛季我准确预测了森林的连续两次解雇。当然格拉斯纳不会是下一个？好吧，继续……
比利·格兰特 Beesotted播客和博客；@Beesotted；@BillyTheBee99
看到西汉姆、切尔西甚至水晶宫在欧会杯一路走到底，我们的主要目标是在那里表现出色，并赢得自1910年慈善盾以来的首个杯赛决赛。我对此乐观吗？并不。今年比赛看起来更难。弗赖堡、亚特兰大和摩纳哥都有真正的欧战经验。甚至对特罗姆瑟的附加赛也是块香蕉皮。我年纪足够大，记得布莱顿在温德米尔湖以北永远赢不了时去卡莱尔的那些可怕旅行。更不用说在真正的北极圈内了。
关键球员/弱点 关键球员将是法比安·许尔策勒用来填补出售丹尼·维尔贝克留下的空缺的人：乔治尼奥·鲁特、查拉兰波斯·科斯图拉斯或斯特凡诺斯·齐马斯。维尔贝克上赛季不仅打进13球，而且大多数是关键的扳平或重要制胜球，价值13分。让他加盟切尔西是巨大的风险。如果俱乐部希望本赛季更多出场的年轻替代者中没有一个站出来取代维尔贝克，那就是弱点。而这三人都有很大的问号。
我们仍需签下…… 从切尔西签下丹尼·维尔贝克将是一个好签约，因为他的进球记录和他会给年轻阵容带来的经验。
我们的崇拜英雄是…… 鲁特。没有什么比一个关于足球生涯的Instagram账户和一个关于你拥有的赛马的账户更能说明崇拜英雄了。而赛马的那个更有趣。
如果我们能从过去签下两名球员…… 我就不再提维尔贝克了，说格伦·穆雷和博比·萨莫拉吧。希望我能在2027年6月3日重新考虑这个问题，那时我们刚刚赢得欧会杯，科斯图拉斯在所有比赛中打入46球。丹尼是谁？
我们将排名第13。前四：1.阿森纳；2.曼联；3.曼城；4.切尔西；后三：18.桑德兰；19.伊普斯维奇；20.赫尔城。首位下课主帅：奥利弗·格拉斯纳。
斯科特·麦卡锡 WeAreBrighton.com
新顶级主帅，一些像样的新签约，队内良好的感觉——很难不乐观。我们终于引进了一些有经验的球员，他们应该补充我们的年轻球员，并将他们提升到下一个水平。没有欧冠比赛，目标必须是前四和在国内杯赛中表现出色。
关键球员/弱点 我们加强了大多数位置，所以新签约快速产生影响是关键。帕尔默和科尔威尔希望能完全康复，并立即进入状态。非常期待看到摩根·罗杰斯穿上蓝衫，马可·帕莱斯特拉看起来很有前途。但我仍然担心桑切斯把守球门，彭德斯可能对英超来说有点青涩。至于年轻人，我会把雷吉·沃森作为外卡加入阵容。他在季前赛给人留下深刻印象，散发着真正的约翰·特里气息。他怎么只有16岁？
我们仍需签下…… 如果恩佐·费尔南德斯离开，他需要被替代；亚历克斯·斯科特和亚当·沃顿都被大量传闻，任何一个都是好选择，增加球队的英格兰脊梁。阵容其他部分看起来非常平衡，有深度。在窗口的这个阶段，主要焦点将是把阵容精简到可控水平。
我们的崇拜英雄是…… 在一支没有多少真正角色的球队中，我希望一些新签约能稍微震撼一下阵容。我有种感觉，佩普·查瓦里亚可能会凭借一些黑暗艺术迅速成为球迷最爱。科尔·帕尔默将继续在场上场下用他出色的采访娱乐大家。
如果我们能从过去签下两名球员…… 约翰·特里来组织防线，弗兰克·兰帕德来进球。这两名球员每次上场都付出100%，也是出色的激励者。两位绝对传奇，在任何时代都能为任何球队增光。
我们将排名第四。前四：1.阿森纳；2.曼联；3.曼城；4.切尔西。后三：18.纽卡斯尔；19.伊普斯维奇；20.赫尔城。首位下课主帅：谢尔盖·亚基罗维奇。
保罗·贝克 纪念特里齐亚·菲奥雷利诺
选择乐观没有坏处，所以是的，我们乐观。我不期望上半区排名，但我确实喜欢俱乐部的运营方式，并相信我们的竞争能力。显然目标是生存，但在其中，如果我们能展示我们的优点并提供挑战，那将是非常可接受的回报。

关键球员/弱点 我们花的钱基本深不可测，但我关注的是那些对我们升级至关重要的球员。马特·格莱姆斯连接了球队中的每个人，所以我们依赖他再次做到这一点，否则我们将不得不发展一种全新的运作方式。签下门将卡尔·拉什沃斯也给后防带来保障，我们希望这能转化为积分。我们的前锋有问题（对于上赛季打进99球的球队来说，这感觉疯狂）。这并不复杂——我们只是不知道赖特和西姆斯是否有能力在最高水平进球。除了签下奥雷尔·阿门达，我们也没有动防线。这是一个大胆的策略。利亚姆·基钦和杰伊·达西尔瓦有了显著进步，但很难忽视我们依赖这样的球员找到另一个上升点的想法。然而，新援卡莱布·伊伦基看起来非常特别。
我们仍需签下…… 我们看到了布莱恩·布罗比上赛季对桑德兰的重要性。一个充满活力的高地位前锋将大大有助于平息对我们前锋线的紧张情绪。泰沃·阿沃尼伊能成为那个人吗？希望如此。关于菲卡约·托莫里的传闻令人兴奋。如果我们能引进他，天哪。
我们的崇拜英雄是…… 虽然回归的格斯·哈默显然是我们崇拜的英雄，但米兰·范埃韦克是球队的活宝。你会在每次庆祝活动中看到他站在最前面。但别让傻气骗了你；他是一个非常非常认真的球员。
如果我们能从过去签下两名球员…… 原始版本的詹姆斯·麦迪逊是我从未见过的。他的比赛随着年龄而改变，这很遗憾，但我想要一些那种早期的创造力。我也欢迎维克托·于厄克雷斯回来。当他相信自己是明星球员时，他发挥得更好。回家吧维克，为考文垂打进至少9个英超进球。
我们将排名第17。前四：1.曼城，2.切尔西，3.阿森纳，4.曼联。后三：18.伊普斯维奇，19.富勒姆，20.赫尔城。首位下课主帅：丹尼尔·法尔克。
尼尔·艾利森 @skybluesblog，Nii Lamptey Show播客
我们期待什么？现在真的很难说。唯一离开的关键球员（到目前为止）是马克桑斯·拉克鲁瓦，我们从他身上赚取了巨额利润，但我们仍然需要加强阵容，以便应对深入欧联杯的严酷考验，同时不危及英超战役——这是上赛季的教训。很多引进交易似乎接近，但尚未完成。
关键球员/弱点 鉴于阵容其他部分缺乏进球，伊斯梅拉·萨尔和J-P·马特塔将再次至关重要。亚当·沃顿将展示图赫尔将他排除在世界杯之外是多么疯狂，蒂里克·米切尔将继续在左路表现出色。杰迪·坎沃特，仍然只有20岁，注定成为一名出色的中卫，本赛季应进一步提升地位。
我们仍需签下…… 已经有一些扎实的交易——美国少年扎维尔·戈佐和右后卫阿南·哈拉伊利看起来令人兴奋的前景，埃万·盖桑德从维拉回归受欢迎。但我们仍然需要拉克鲁瓦的替代者，以及中场的实力——我们3500万英镑报价摩纳哥的拉明·卡马拉被拒绝。还有很多事要做。与此同时，用德怀特·麦克尼尔交换布伦南·约翰逊的决定存在分歧：约翰逊——所有3500万英镑——只在这里待了几个月。
我们的崇拜英雄是…… 有几个竞争者。马特塔，显然，领唱迪恩·亨德森，以及可能我们的巴西攻击手马特乌斯·弗兰萨。他还没到那一步，但他在三年前19岁时加盟，由于各种原因几乎没有产生影响。但他有一个强劲的季前赛，包括跳舞进球庆祝——一些巴西风情会在塞尔赫斯特很受欢迎。
如果我们能从过去签下两名球员…… 迈克尔·奥利塞毫无疑问；他在水晶宫显然是世界级球员，并继续惊人地进步。还有90年代末的马特·詹森——我的个人英雄；如此年轻就有如此惊人的天赋，会在现代闪耀。

关键球员/弱点 刘易斯·迈利是“我们自己人”，随着托纳利离开，他可以发挥潜力。我们也期待门将位置的改进，卢卡斯·霍尔尼切克和尤恩·雅乌恩竞争门将球衣。如果约阿内·维萨和安东尼·埃兰加能复制世界杯状态，我们可能有了一个锋线组合。弱点？乔·威洛克，上赛季对事业贡献甚微，以及不幸的斯文·博特曼，他的状态从未从2024年的前十字韧带伤病中恢复。
我们仍需签下…… 布鲁诺·吉马良斯的替代者，场上场下的领袖，两个边后卫位置的高质量替补，一名中卫……所以要求不多……本菲卡的多面手边后卫阿马尔·德迪奇和米兰的中卫菲卡约·托莫里肯定是一个好的开始。至关重要的是，我们需要为年轻阵容融入更多经验，但鉴于利物浦最近的行为，任何交易都必须以隐身模式进行……
我们的崇拜英雄是…… 大丹·伯恩。一个巨人，心也匹配。
如果我们能从过去签下两名球员…… 阿兰·希勒，因为他的领导力和进球，当然还有深受喜爱和怀念的凯文·基冈。两人都知道穿上黑白球衣意味着什么。
我们将排名第10。前四：1.阿森纳；2.曼城；3.利物浦；4.切尔西。后三：18.伊普斯维奇；19.考文垂；20.赫尔城。首位下课主帅：阿尔瓦罗·阿韦洛亚。
大卫和理查德·霍姆斯
如果不出意外，不会像上赛季那样混乱。我们最终相当轻松地保级——谢谢维托尔！——然后解雇他，选择格拉斯纳，理由是这个奥地利人赢得过奖杯。所以这次的目标不仅是联赛排名不错，而且还要有奖杯入柜。

bodyEn: The doubt for anyone when a long-strived-for goal has been achieved is hunger. Arsenal waited 22 years for their 14th league title and, compounding the yearning, finished second three times in a row before finally lifting the Premier League trophy in May. The physical exertions of last season were immense – as seen by Declan Rice’s clear exhaustion and Bukayo Saka’s intermittent contributions at the World Cup, where William Saliba picked up a back injury – but so too was the emotional strain.

The first weeks of a new season after a major tournament, especially the World Cup, are often a little erratic anyway, but this feels like a particularly unpredictable start to a campaign. Nine of the 20 Premier League clubs have changed manager this summer. For the first time in 40 years, none of the five big managerial beasts of the Premier League era – Sir Alex Ferguson, Arsène Wenger, José Mourinho, Jürgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola – will be in charge of a club. There are unknowns and uncertainty everywhere, even at Arsenal. Mikel Arteta may be the longest-serving manager in the league but there are questions even there; it would be no great surprise if Arsenal were to start slowly.

Manchester City are at the other end of the scale, after two seasons that were disappointing by their extremely elevated recent standards, and with a new manager after a decade under Guardiola. Enzo Maresca may look like his predecessor and his football may look like a version of his predecessor’s – notably from that period when he was his assistant manager – but he arrives at City surrounded by questions. He led Leicester to promotion and won the Europa Conference League and Club World Cup with Chelsea, but fans of those clubs seemed unconvinced by the style of play. And while Chelsea clearly had problems with the balance of their squad, and got dramatically worse after he left, it wasn’t entirely clear he was making the best of the resources he had.

The Community Shield is a first opportunity to make some kind of assessment of whether Arsenal’s hunger is as sharp as it was last season, and of how City’s squad are adapting to their new manager. It is, though, a largely ceremonial occasion, any lessons drawn to be taken with extreme caution. Not since 2018 have the winners of the Community Shield gone on to win the Premier League; in that sense, it’s a sort of anti-bellwether. Where it can give indicators as to the season ahead tends to be less in showcasing the strengths of a potential champion than in exposing the flaws that might bring a side low.

This year is unlikely to bring a repeat of 1974, when the scrap between Kevin Keegan and Billy Bremner exposed both the Liverpool forward’s unease at the retirement of Bill Shankly and, more consequentially, the general loss of morale at Leeds after Brian Clough had succeeded Don Revie. Often the significance of the Community Shield is properly recognised only in retrospect. José Mourinho was clearly in a strange mood when he turned up for the 2015-16 game unshaven and in tracksuit bottoms and a baggy T-shirt before suffering his first ever defeat to Arsène Wenger. Few suspected, though, the chaos that was about to unspool at Chelsea, culminating with Mourinho’s dismissal that December.

Last season, as Crystal Palace beat Liverpool on penalties after a 2-2 draw, there were abundant indications of what was to come, especially about Arne Slot’s side. Mohamed Salah seemed disconnected from the rest of the forward line. The defence was a mess. Twice they conceded equalisers. Whether they were recognised at the time is another matter; the difficulty is separating teething problems or a team being only partway through their preparation for the new season from longer-term issues that could still be undermining a team two or three months into the season.

There are few obvious questions to which Sunday’s meeting could begin to offer answers. Bruno Guimarães came off the bench for Arsenal in Wednesday’s friendly against Como and could be involved, probably alongside Myles Lewis-Skelly in midfield. The 19-year-old has been prominent in pre-season after Declan Rice, Martín Zubimendi and Martin Ødegaard were given extended breaks after the World Cup, but he has been linked with a move. In that context, his celebration after scoring against Como, making a heart sign with his hands and tapping the badge, felt significant.

After the sale of Leandro Trossard, the left side of Arsenal’s attack is in need of strengthening. Morgan Rogers went to Chelsea and Vinícius Júnior stayed at Real Madrid, but they did sign the 24-year-old Greece international Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge. Sunday offers an opportunity to see how he fits in, and whether Arsenal still need another option on that flank.

For City, the biggest personnel issue probably surrounds the future of Rodri, whose proposed move to Barcelona is yet to materialise, which in turn leaves City hanging on a potential replacement. Enzo Fernández appears the preferred candidate but whether his comparative lack of physicality can be accommodated deep in midfield, even after the signing of the robust Elliot Anderson, remains to be seen.

Tijjani Reijnders started friendlies against Inter and Atlético but is on his way to Al-Qadsiah while Bernardo Silva has joined Real Madrid, meaning a significant overhaul of midfield. Whether that includes Phil Foden in the long term is unclear. Since being named player of the year in 2024, he has struggled for form, but started the Inter and Atlético games. As others recover from the World Cup, the next few weeks offer an opportunity to reassert himself.

Given he started only 11 games over the past two seasons, the departure of John Stones probably matters less from a footballing point of view than in the loss of a dressing-room leader. Without Stones and Silva – and Guardiola – the character of the squad cannot but be different.

Sunday constitutes an opportunity to see both what the new City may look like, and how Arsenal have adapted, having at last won the title. But it’s only the Community Shield; any conclusions should be treated with appropriate caution.

items.titleZh: 社区盾杯揭示阿森纳的渴望与马雷斯卡对曼城的影响 | 乔纳森·威尔逊
items.summaryZh: 社区盾杯或露端倪，但并非赛季可靠指标，其冠军自2018年起未再夺英超。
bodyZh: 当一个人长期奋斗的目标终于实现时，随之而来的疑问便是饥饿感。阿森纳等待了22年才夺得第14座联赛冠军，而在最终于五月捧起英超奖杯之前，他们连续三次屈居亚军，这更加剧了渴望。上赛季的体能消耗巨大——从德克兰·赖斯的明显疲惫和布卡约·萨卡在世界杯上的断断续续表现中可见一斑，威廉·萨利巴还在此次赛事中背部受伤——但情感上的压力同样巨大。

重大赛事（尤其是世界杯）之后的新赛季头几周，通常总有些不太稳定，但本赛季的开局感觉格外难以预料。20支英超俱乐部中有9支在夏天更换了主教练。40年来首次，英超时代的五位顶级主帅——亚历克斯·弗格森爵士、阿尔塞纳·温格、何塞·穆里尼奥、尤尔根·克洛普和佩普·瓜迪奥拉——均不再执掌任何俱乐部。到处都存在着未知与不确定性，即便是阿森纳也不例外。米克尔·阿尔特塔或许是联赛中执教时间最长的主教练，但即便在他那里也存在疑问；如果阿森纳开局缓慢，也不足为奇。

曼城则处于另一个极端，经历了两个按他们极高近年标准来看令人失望的赛季后，在瓜迪奥拉执教十年之后迎来了新帅。恩佐·马雷斯卡或许看起来像他的前任，他的足球或许也像前任的某种版本——尤其是他担任助理教练的那段时期——但他接手曼城时也伴随着众多问号。他曾带领莱斯特城升级，并与切尔西一起赢得了欧会杯和世俱杯，但那些俱乐部的球迷似乎对其比赛风格并不信服。尽管切尔西在阵容平衡上显然存在问题，且在他离开后情况急剧恶化，但尚不完全清楚他是否充分利用了手头的资源。
社区盾杯是评估阿森纳的渴望是否仍如去年一样强烈、以及曼城阵容如何适应新帅的第一次机会。然而，这大体上是一个仪式性的场合，从中得出的任何结论都应格外谨慎。自2018年以来，还没有社区盾杯冠军最终赢得英超联赛；从这个意义上说，它像是一种反风向标。它能对接下来赛季提供的指示，往往不在于展示潜在冠军的优势，而在于暴露可能让球队陷入低谷的缺陷。

今年不太可能重演1974年的情形，当时凯文·基冈和比利·布雷姆纳之间的冲突既暴露了利物浦前锋对比尔·香克利退役的不安，更重要的是，也揭示了利兹联在布莱恩·克劳夫接替唐·雷维后整体士气的低落。社区盾杯的意义往往只有在回顾时才能被正确认识。何塞·穆里尼奥在2015-16赛季的比赛中出场时胡子拉碴、穿着运动裤和宽松T恤，显然处于一种奇怪的情绪中，随后他遭遇了对阿尔塞纳·温格的首场失利。不过，很少有人预料到切尔西即将爆发的混乱，最终导致穆里尼奥在当年12月被解雇。
上赛季，水晶宫在2-2战平后点球击败利物浦，那场比赛对于未来有大量暗示，尤其是关于阿尔内·斯洛特的球队。穆罕默德·萨拉赫似乎与锋线其他球员脱节。防守一团糟。他们两次被扳平。当时这些迹象是否被认识到是另一回事；难点在于区分暂时性问题或球队仅完成了部分赛季准备，与那些可能在赛季进行两三个月后仍困扰球队的长期问题。
周日的对决几乎没有什么明确的问题能开始给出答案。布鲁诺·吉马良斯在周三对阵科莫的友谊赛中替补出场为阿森纳登场，他可能会出场，很可能与迈尔斯·刘易斯-斯凯利一起出现在中场。这位19岁的小将在德克兰·赖斯、马丁·苏比门迪和马丁·厄德高在世界杯后被延长假期后，在季前赛中表现突出，但他一直被与转会传闻联系在一起。在这种情况下，他对科莫进球后的庆祝动作——双手比心并拍打队徽——显得意味深长。
在出售莱安德罗·特罗萨德之后，阿森纳进攻的左侧需要加强。摩根·罗杰斯去了切尔西，维尼修斯·儒尼奥尔留在了皇家马德里，但他们从布鲁日签下了24岁的希腊国脚克里斯托斯·佐利斯。周日将提供一个机会来观察他如何融入，以及阿森纳是否仍需要该侧翼的另一个选择。
对曼城而言，最大的人员问题可能围绕罗德里 的未来，他转会巴塞罗那的提议尚未成行，这反过来使曼城对潜在替代者悬而未决。恩佐·费尔南德斯似乎是首选候选人，但即使签下了强壮的埃利奥特·安德森，他相对缺乏身体对抗能力是否能在中场深处被容纳，仍有待观察。
订阅《足球每日》
以《卫报》对足球世界的看法开启你的夜晚
在通讯推广之后
蒂贾尼·赖恩德斯在对阵国际米兰和马德里竞技的友谊赛中首发，但他即将前往阿尔卡迪西亚，而贝尔纳多·席尔瓦已加盟皇家马德里，这意味着中场将经历重大改革。长期来看这是否包括菲尔·福登尚不清楚。自2024年当选年度最佳球员以来，他一直状态挣扎，但他在对阵国际米兰和马竞的比赛中首发。随着其他球员从世界杯中恢复，接下来几周是他重新证明自己的机会。
鉴于他过去两个赛季只首发了11场比赛，约翰·斯通斯的离开从足球角度来看可能没有失去更衣室领袖那么重要。没有斯通斯和席尔瓦——也没有瓜迪奥拉——球队的性格不可能不发生改变。
周日既是一个观察新曼城可能面貌的机会，也是一个观察阿森纳在终于赢得冠军后如何调整的机会。但这只是社区盾杯；任何结论都应谨慎对待。

items.titleEn: Ismeal Kabia joins St Mirren on loan
items.summaryEn: Our young attacker is heading to Scotland for the 2026/27
bodyEn: Ismeal Kabia has joined Scottish Premiership side St Mirren on a season-long loan.
The 20-year-old joined our academy in March 2017 and signed his first professional contract with us in July 2024.
An impressive 2024/25 campaign saw Ismeal make his first-team debut for us in our 5-1 win against Bolton Wanderers in the Carabao Cup third round at Emirates Stadium.

Standout performances led to Ismeal signing a second professional contract with us in August 2025, shortly followed by a loan move to Shrewsbury Town for the 2025/26 season. A valuable spell for the Dutch-born winger, who made 43 appearances across all competitions for the League Two side.
We wish Ismeal all the best for his loan spell at St Mirren and look forward to seeing his continued development.
The loan deal is subject to the completion of regulatory processes.

items.titleZh: 伊斯梅尔·卡比亚租借加盟圣米伦
items.summaryZh: 我们的年轻攻击手将前往苏格兰参加2026/27赛季。
bodyZh: 伊斯梅尔·卡比亚已租借加盟苏格兰超级联赛球队圣米伦，租期为一个赛季。
这位20岁的球员于2017年3月加入我们的青训营，并于2024年7月与我们签下了他的第一份职业合同。
在令人印象深刻的2024/25赛季中，伊斯梅尔在酋长球场对阵博尔顿流浪者的联赛杯第三轮比赛中完成了我们的一线队首秀，帮助球队以5-1获胜。
出色的表现让伊斯梅尔在2025年8月与我们签下了第二份职业合同，随后不久便被租借至什鲁斯伯里镇，出战2025/26赛季。对于这位荷兰出生的边锋来说，这是一段宝贵的经历，他为这支英乙球队在各项赛事中共出场43次。
我们祝愿伊斯梅尔在圣米伦的租借生涯一切顺利，并期待看到他的持续成长。

items.titleEn: Principality Perfection: Our best wins in Cardiff
items.summaryEn: We take a look back at some of the classic victories in Cardiff down the years
bodyEn: After almost 20 years, we're returning to the Principality Stadium as we take on Manchester City in the Community Shield.
The ground became a home away from home for Arsene Wenger's side, winning the FA Cup on three occasions as well as picking up two Community Shields.
As we get set to make our return, here's a look at some of our classic victories in Cardiff!
PARLOUR'S PEARLER
Arsenal 2-0 Chelsea - FA Cup final, May 2002
We headed to Cardiff in May 2002 to take on Chelsea in the FA Cup final as we looked to complete part one of a historic double.

After a tight first half, we broke the deadlock with 20 minutes to play with one of the all-time classic FA Cup final goals. Midfielder Ray Parlour picked the ball up in space and unleashed a shot beyond Carlo Cudicini and into the top corner.
The game was sealed 10 minutes later with another belter, this time from Freddie Ljungberg, curling into the net. Four days later, we won the Premier League to clinch our second double.
PIRES WINS THE CUP
Arsenal 1-0 Southampton - FA Cup final, May 2003
A year on from our Chelsea triumph, we were back in Cardiff looking to defend the trophy against Southampton.
With the roof on at the Principality Stadium, Robert Pires scored the game's decisive goal to help us to back-to-back.
The game was David Seaman's last as a Gunner, bringing an end to his momentous 13-year spell in north London.
PENALTY DRAMA
Arsenal (5-4 pens) 0-0 Manchester United - FA Cup final, May 2005
Having missed out on the FA Cup in 2004, we returned to Cardiff in 2005 to take on holders Manchester United.
In a display of resilience, we stood firm against the Red Devils' attack as the game went to extra time, where we were reduced to 10 players after Jose Antonio Reyes was shown a second yellow.
We forced the game to penalties, where Jens Lehmann denied Paul Scholes, allowing Patrick Vieira to fire home his spot kick to seal the title.
REYES BEATS REDS
Arsenal 3-1 Manchester United - Community Shield, August 2004
After completing our Invincibles campaign, our first game of the new season saw us up against Manchester United in the Community Shield curtain-raiser in Cardiff.
Having scored the winner in the 2002 edition, Gilberto opened the scoring before Alan Smith equalised for Sir Alex Ferguson's men.

Jose Antonio Reyes delivered a player of the match performance in the Welsh capital, finding the net to make it 2-1 before Ashley Cole's pass was deflected into his own net by Mikael Silvestre to give us the perfect start to 2024/05.
RVP AT THE DOUBLE
Arsenal 3-0 Blackburn Rovers, FA Cup semi-final, April 2005
The 2005 FA Cup semi-finals were hosted at the Principality Stadium for the first and only time, as we took on Blackburn Rovers for a chance to reach the final.
We broke the deadlock three minutes before half-time after good work from Kolo Toure found Pires to put us ahead.
Robin van Persie then stole the show, scoring a fine individual goal before his curling effort went beyond Brad Freidel to give us a 3-0 win and set up a final with Manchester United.

帕洛尔的绝妙进球
阿森纳2-0切尔西 - 2002年5月足总杯决赛
2002年5月，我们前往卡迪夫，在足总杯决赛中对阵切尔西，目标是完成历史性双冠王的第一步。
上半场双方战平，第20分钟，我们凭借一粒足总杯决赛历史上的经典进球打破僵局。中场球员雷·帕洛尔在空当处接球，一脚射门越过卡罗·库迪奇尼，直挂死角。
10分钟后，另一粒精彩进球锁定了胜局，这次是弗雷迪·永贝里的弧线球入网。四天后，我们赢得英超冠军，完成了我们的第二次双冠王。
皮雷斯捧起奖杯
阿森纳1-0南安普顿 - 2003年5月足总杯决赛
在战胜切尔西一年后，我们重返卡迪夫，对阵南安普顿，卫冕奖杯。
在公国球场关顶的情况下，罗伯特·皮雷斯打入了比赛的决定性进球，帮助我们实现了卫冕。
这场比赛是大卫·希曼作为枪手的最后一场比赛，结束了他长达13年的北伦敦生涯。
点球大战
阿森纳（5-4点球）0-0曼联 - 2005年5月足总杯决赛
在2004年无缘足总杯之后，我们于2005年重返卡迪夫，对阵卫冕冠军曼联。
我们展现出了顽强的韧性，在红魔的进攻面前坚守阵地，比赛进入加时赛，而我们在何塞·安东尼奥·雷耶斯吃到第二张黄牌后被罚下，只剩下10人应战。
我们顽强地将比赛拖入点球大战，延斯·莱曼扑出了保罗·斯科尔斯的点球，随后帕特里克·维埃拉主罚命中，锁定冠军。
雷耶斯击败红魔
阿森纳3-1曼联 - 2004年8月社区盾
在完成不败赛季之后，我们新赛季的首场比赛是在卡迪夫举行的社区盾揭幕战中对阵曼联。
在2002年的比赛中打入制胜球的吉尔伯托首开纪录，随后阿兰·史密斯为弗格森爵士的球队扳平比分。
何塞·安东尼奥·雷耶斯在威尔士首都奉献了全场最佳表现，他打入一球将比分改写为2-1，随后阿什利·科尔的传球被米卡埃尔·西尔维斯特乌龙挡入自家球门，为我们开启了2024-05赛季的完美开局（注：原文为2004/05，此处照译）。
范佩西梅开二度
阿森纳3-0布莱克本流浪者 - 2005年4月足总杯半决赛
2005年足总杯半决赛首次也是唯一一次在公国球场举行，我们与布莱克本流浪者队争夺决赛资格。
半场结束前三分钟，科洛·图雷的精妙配合找到了皮雷斯，后者为我们取得领先，打破了僵局。
随后罗宾·范佩西大放异彩，他先是一记精彩的个人进球，随后一记弧线球越过布拉德·弗里德尔，为我们带来3-0的胜利，并确保与曼联会师决赛。

bodyEn: Mikel Arteta has said he is relaxed about his Arsenal contract expiring at the end of the new season and believes his side will need to be better than last year to defend their title successfully.

The Premier League champions will face Enzo Maresca’s Manchester City in the Community Shield in Cardiff on Sunday and are heavy favourites to win back-to-back league titles for the first time since the 1930s. The departure of Pep Guardiola from their traditional rivals City means Arteta is now the Premier League’s longest-serving manager, with the Spaniard having joined in December 2019.

He signed a three-year contract extension in September 2024 after Arsenal finished as runners-up to City and had been expected to agree a new deal over the summer that would make him one of the highest-paid managers in the world. Arteta acknowledged on Friday that his priorities have been elsewhere this summer as he attempts to strengthen his squad before the new season but reassured supporters that he is fully committed to the club.

“They don’t have to worry about any of that, because I want to be here. I am extremely happy. I feel very grateful to work with the people that I work with and when we have the possibility, we will resolve that. And that’s it,” he said.

Asked if he expects talks over a new contract to continue after the transfer window, Arteta added: “There is always another priority, I think. And that’s the way we have been treating it, I think because everybody feels comfortable that the time on the contract is not going to be an issue. I think because my will, certainly, is to be here and I am very happy here. My feeling from the club is the same one. That is why everyone is doing things in a really organic way.”

Arsenal have opened negotiations with Bayer Leverkusen over a move for Jarell Quansah as they seek cover for William Saliba and Jurriën Timber, while they are still in the market for another attacker if they can offload Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus. After missing out on Vinícius Júnior when the Brazil forward opted to sign a new deal with Real Madrid, Arteta defended Arsenal’s strategy this summer and is hoping that they can still add to their squad.

“I am really happy with the squad, the players that I have and I am really happy with the ambition of the club. There is zero question about that. We have shown that in the manner we have tried to act,” he said.

“But I think we need to do it our own way. We have super strengths and we have other areas we need to be very conscious [of] because we don’t have the elements or the structure that other clubs have. We need to do it our way. We are always on it that way and we will do what we believe is the right thing to do. To have the best possibility to compete in every competition that’s for sure.”

items.titleZh: “不会成为问题”：阿尔特塔对阿森纳合同情况感到放松
items.summaryZh: 阿尔特塔表示对合同到期感到放松，并称球队需比去年更出色。
bodyZh: 米克尔·阿尔特塔表示，他对自己的阿森纳合同将在新赛季结束后到期感到放松，并认为球队需要比去年表现得更好才能成功卫冕冠军。
英超冠军将在周日的社区盾杯中于加的夫对阵恩佐·马雷斯卡执教的曼城，并且是自20世纪30年代以来首次连续夺得联赛冠军的热门球队。佩普·瓜迪奥拉离开传统对手曼城，意味着阿尔特塔现在是英超执教时间最长的主教练，这位西班牙人于2019年12月加盟。
他在2024年9月签署了一份为期三年的续约合同，此前阿森纳在联赛中排名第二，落后于曼城，而外界预计他将在夏季达成新协议，使他成为世界上薪酬最高的主教练之一。阿尔特塔在周五承认，这个夏天他的优先事项放在了其他地方，因为他试图在新赛季前增强阵容，但他向支持者保证，他对俱乐部完全投入。
“他们不必为此担心，因为我想留在这里。我非常开心。我非常感激能与我共事的人一起工作，当我们有机会时，我们会解决这个问题。就这样，”他说。
在被问及是否预计转会窗口结束后会继续就新合同进行谈判时，阿尔特塔补充道：“我认为总有另一个优先事项。我们一直是这么对待的，因为大家都觉得合同时间不会成为问题。当然，因为我的意愿是留在这里，而且我在这里非常开心。俱乐部给我的感觉也是一样的。这就是为什么每个人都在以非常自然的方式做事。”
阿森纳已与勒沃库森就雅雷尔·昆萨的转会展开谈判，以寻求威廉·萨利巴和尤里安·廷贝尔的替补，同时他们仍在市场上寻找另一名攻击手，前提是能出售加布里埃尔·马丁内利和加布里埃尔·热苏斯。在维尼修斯·儒尼奥尔选择与皇家马德里续约而错失他之后，阿尔特塔为阿森纳今年夏天的策略进行了辩护，并希望他们仍能补充阵容。
“我对阵容、现有的球员以及俱乐部的雄心感到非常满意。这一点毫无疑问。我们已经通过我们的行动方式表明了这一点，”他说。
“但我认为我们需要用自己的方式做事。我们有超强的优势，也有其他领域需要非常谨慎，因为我们没有其他俱乐部所拥有的要素或结构。我们需要走自己的路。我们一直在这样做，我们会做我们认为正确的事情。为了在每个赛事中都有最好的竞争机会，这一点是肯定的。”

bodyEn: Arsenal have opened talks with Bayer Leverkusen over a move for Jarell Quansah as they intensify efforts to bring in cover for William Saliba and Jurriën Timber.

The England defender, who left Liverpool last summer for an initial £30m and was part of Thomas Tuchel’s World Cup squad, has been identified as an ideal replacement for the France and Netherlands defenders, who will miss the start of the new season due to injury. While Quansah’s preferred position is in central defence, he was also deployed at right-back by Tuchel at the World Cup and was sent off in the last-16 victory over Mexico.

It is understood that Leverkusen are reluctant to sell the Warrington-born 23-year-old, who signed a five-year deal when he left Anfield last July, and would want at least €50m (£43m). Arsenal – who saw a bid of £30m for Aston Villa’s Ezri Konsa rejected earlier in the window – are not thought to want to pay that much but now could test the German club’s resolve by submitting a similar offer. Liverpool had a €70m buyback option on Quansah but that has now expired.
Arsenal are still believed to be interested in Konsa, who also filled in at right-back for England during the World Cup but is better known as a central defender. Villa value the 28-year-old at £60m.

Mikel Arteta said this week that Saliba’s back injury would take “some time to heal” and he was unsure about when he would be available again. Arsenal also have concerns over Timber, who pulled out of the Netherlands squad on the eve of the World Cup after failing to recover from a persistent groin injury that forced him to miss most of the run‑in last season.

“Jurriën is progressing really well,” Arteta said after Arsenal’s friendly defeat by Borussia ­Dortmund last Sunday. “He’s on the pitch, he’s doing quite a lot right now, but it’s still weeks away. I cannot tell you how much.”

Arsenal would still like to sign a new attacker before the end of the window and could allow Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus to depart in order to free up more funds. ­Galatasaray have offered £38m for Martinelli, although the Brazil ­forward has turned down a move to Turkey. Napoli have shown an ­interest in Jesus.
Ethan Nwaneri could also be sold, with Milan, Fulham, RB Leipzig and Borussia Dortmund among those who have been linked with the 19-year-old.

items.titleZh: 阿森纳就贾雷尔·宽萨的转会与勒沃库森展开谈判
items.summaryZh: 阿森纳与勒沃库森就宽萨转会展开谈判，对方要价至少5000万欧元，枪手仍有意孔萨。
bodyZh: 阿森纳已与勒沃库森就贾雷尔·宽萨的转会展开谈判，以加强为威廉·萨利巴和尤里安·廷贝尔寻找替补的努力。
这位英格兰后卫去年夏天以3000万英镑初始转会费离开利物浦，并入选了托马斯·图赫尔的世界杯大名单。他被视为因伤将缺席新赛季开局的法国和荷兰后卫的理想替代者。尽管宽萨的首选位置是中后卫，但图赫尔在世界杯上也让他出任右后卫，在16强战胜墨西哥的比赛中他还被红牌罚下。
据悉，勒沃库森不愿出售这位出生于沃灵顿的23岁球员，他在去年7月离开安菲尔德时签下了一份五年合同，德甲俱乐部希望至少得到5000万欧元（4300万英镑）。阿森纳在转会窗口早些时候为阿斯顿维拉的埃兹里·孔萨开出的3000万英镑报价已被拒绝，人们认为他们不想支付那么多，但现在可能会提交类似的报价来考验这家德国俱乐部的决心。利物浦曾拥有对宽萨的7000万欧元回购条款，但该条款现已过期。
据信阿森纳仍对孔萨感兴趣，他在世界杯期间也为英格兰队客串过右后卫，但更出名的是中后卫。维拉对这位28岁球员的估价为6000万英镑。
米克尔·阿尔特塔本周表示，萨利巴的背部伤病“需要一些时间才能痊愈”，他也不确定后者何时能再次上场。阿森纳也对廷贝尔感到担忧，他在世界杯前夕因腹股沟持续伤病未能恢复而退出荷兰队，上赛季他因此缺席了大部分收官阶段的比赛。
“尤里安恢复得很好，”阿尔特塔在上周日阿森纳友谊赛输给多特蒙德后表示。“他已经回到球场，目前做大量训练，但距离复出还有数周。我无法告诉你具体还要多久。”
阿森纳仍希望在转会窗口结束前签下一名新攻击手，并可能放走加布里埃尔·马丁内利和加布里埃尔·热苏斯以腾出更多资金。加拉塔萨雷已为马丁内利开出3800万英镑的报价，不过这位巴西前锋拒绝了前往土耳其的转会。那不勒斯对热苏斯表现出了兴趣。
伊桑·恩瓦内里也可能被出售，米兰、富勒姆、RB莱比锡和多特蒙德都与这位19岁小将传出绯闻。

迈尔斯·刘易斯-斯凯利的未来尚不明朗，本周他被推荐给了切尔西和曼联。阿尔特塔周三在友谊赛对阵科莫（由塞斯克·法布雷加斯执教）的比赛中进球后，拒绝回应这些传闻。
“我不会谈论猜测，”他说。“如果我们的球员有传闻，那是个好兆头。这意味着我们的球员引人关注，并且表现出色。”

bodyEn: Curtis Jones’s future has been the subject of much gossipmongering this summer, especially with Inter plonking him in the middle of their radar. The Italian club have sniffed around the midfielder for quite a while and may ramp up their interest very soon with a bid of £30m to test Liverpool’s resolve.

Ipswich are not willing to stop their summer spending and a return for Julio Enciso looks nailed on. The Paraguay international had an injury-plagued loan spell at Portman Road in 2025 but is back to lead their battle for Premier League survival after a permanent deal was agreed with Strasbourg. Also making the move from the French club is right-back Abdoul Ouattara.

Crystal Palace have been knocked back by Monaco with a £35m bid for midfielder Lamine Camara. The Ligue 1 club are not particularly keen to sell him after getting a decent whack for Aladji Bamba, ensuring their finances are very healthy.

It may be the case that Arsenal need to sell a few players on, as is the case with Myles Lewis-Skelly. Another available player is Gabriel Martinelli who is attracting interest from Galatasaray. The Turkish giants are willing to splash a whopping £38m on the Brazilian. Gala are taking a keen look at Premier League players, with Liverpool’s Alexis Mac Allister another wanted.

After completing a deal for Lucas Herrington, Hull will bring in Joe Gelhardt from Leeds. The forward spent time on loan with the Tigers, helping them get promoted to the Premier League. Another inquiry has been made to Juventus over the availability of Teun Koopmeiners.

Aston Villa are priming themselves for a busy end to the window. João Palhinha has agreed to join on loan but Bayern Munich are eager to sell him. Jonathan David may also turn up in the West Midlands after the Villans got on the blower to Juventus.

Aaron Wan-Bissaka may not fancy a season in the second tier with West Ham. Thankfully for the DR Congo full-back Aston Villa and Fulham are both in for him at the moment, but Villa Park is the more likely destination. On the other side of the Hammers defence is El Hadji Malick Diouf. Sunderland have put a figure on him with a £40m bid but that is not enough for him to be allowed to head up to the Stadium of Light because his employers want £10m more.

Kyle Walker was a target for David Moyes a year ago and the Scot could offer him a route out of Burnley to Everton. The former England right-back has a year remaining on his contract but may fancy a season on Merseyside.

items.titleZh: 足球转会传闻：加拉塔萨雷豪掷3800万英镑求购阿森纳的马丁内利？
items.summaryZh: 今日传闻偏爱邦妮·泰勒版本， Curtis Jones 的未来成焦点。
bodyZh: 柯蒂斯·琼斯的未来今夏成为众多流言的主题，尤其是国际米兰将他列入重点引援目标。这家意大利俱乐部对这位中场球员觊觎已久，可能很快就会以3000万英镑的报价试探利物浦的决心，从而加大兴趣。
伊普斯维奇不愿停止今夏的引援步伐，胡利奥·恩西索的回归看似板上钉钉。这位巴拉圭国脚2025年在波特曼路球场的租借期饱受伤病困扰，但在与斯特拉斯堡达成永久转会后，他将回归带领球队为英超保级而战。同样从这家法国俱乐部加盟的还有右后卫阿卜杜勒·瓦塔拉。
水晶宫以3500万英镑报价摩纳哥中场拉明·卡马拉，但遭到拒绝。这家法甲俱乐部在出售阿莱吉·班巴后获得可观收入，财政状况良好，因此并不特别急于将他出售。
阿森纳可能需要出售一些球员，比如迈尔斯·刘易斯-斯凯利。另一位可出售的球员是加布里埃尔·马丁内利，他引起了加拉塔萨雷的兴趣。这家土耳其豪门愿意为这位巴西人豪掷3800万英镑。加拉塔萨雷正在密切关注英超球员，利物浦的亚历克西斯·麦卡利斯特也是目标之一。
在完成卢卡斯·赫林顿的交易后，赫尔城将从利兹联引进乔·格尔哈特。这位前锋曾租借效力于老虎队，帮助球队升入英超。此外，他们还就特恩·科普梅纳斯的可用性向尤文图斯进行了询问。
阿斯顿维拉正为转会窗结束前的忙碌做准备。若昂·帕利尼亚已同意租借加盟，但拜仁慕尼黑渴望将他出售。乔纳森·戴维也可能出现在西米德兰兹，因为维拉已经联系了尤文图斯。
阿隆·万-比萨卡可能不愿随西汉姆联征战英冠赛季。对这位刚果民主共和国边后卫来说，幸运的是阿斯顿维拉和富勒姆目前都在追求他，但维拉公园是更可能的目的地。西汉姆防线另一侧的目标是埃尔·哈吉·马利克·迪乌夫。桑德兰已报价4000万英镑求购他，但这不足以让他加盟光明球场，因为其东家想要再多1000万英镑。
凯尔·沃克一年前曾是戴维·莫耶斯的目标，这位苏格兰教练可能为他提供离开伯恩利转投埃弗顿的出路。这位前英格兰右后卫的合同还剩一年，但他可能愿意在默西塞德度过一个赛季。
